subject: Decision Making
title: The Tragedy of the Commons
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Tragedy of the Commons usable.

hook.text: A shared pasture is open to all herders. Each adds one more cow because the benefit is private but the cost is shared.

buildup.text: Each herder's decision is rational individually. But when everyone adds cows, the pasture is destroyed for all.

discovery.text: Overfishing, pollution, and traffic jams are all tragedies of the commons. Shared resources invite overuse.

twist.text: Elinor Ostrom won the Nobel Prize for showing communities can manage commons without government.

climax.text: The tragedy is not inevitable. Groups that communicate, monitor, and sanction members can sustain shared resources.

punchline.text: One more cow ruins the pasture. Shared costs with private gains destroy commons.

quiz.question: What causes the tragedy of the commons?
options: Individual gains are private while costs are shared, leading to overuse
